draft.title: Narratives in many forms
card: A story can be told in many forms: prose, poetry, film, graphic novels, podcasts, games and social media posts.
Each form has its own tools. Film uses camera angles, music and editing. A graphic novel uses panels, images and speech bubbles.
A podcast has no pictures, so it relies on voice, sound effects and silence. Prose relies on words, such as description and sentence rhythm.
The same story can feel different in a different form, because the tools shape what the audience sees, hears and notices.
draft.remember: The form of a story decides which tools the creator can use to shape the audience's experience.

a.q: Which pair correctly matches a form with a tool it uses?
opts: Graphic novel and panels
Podcast and camera angles
Prose and speech bubbles
Film and sound effects only
a.why: A graphic novel tells its story through panels laid out on the page. A podcast has no pictures, so camera angles do not belong to it. Film does use sound, but it also uses camera angles and editing, so 'only' is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what the audience can see in each form.

b.q: Kai turns a short story about a storm at sea into a podcast. The audience cannot see the waves. Which tool would best build the danger of the storm?
opts: Sound effects of crashing waves and howling wind
A close-up camera angle on the ship's deck
A page of panels showing the ship tilting
A long paragraph describing the sea's colours
b.why: A podcast works through sound, so crashing waves and wind let listeners imagine the storm. A camera angle and panels need images, which a podcast does not have. A written paragraph is a tool of prose, not of audio.
b.clue: Which tool works when the audience can only listen?

b.best: Sound effects of crashing waves and howling wind

problems.detail: The option 'Film and sound effects only' is ambiguous. Film does use sound effects, so the pairing itself is a correct match. Whether it is wrong depends on reading 'only' as 'film uses nothing but sound effects', and a student could reasonably defend it. Replace it with a clearly wrong pairing.

Why (b) says a paragraph is 'a tool of prose, not of audio'. But the card says a podcast relies on voice, and a narrator can read descriptive language aloud. The distractor works because it describes colours, which listeners cannot see, not because spoken description has no place in audio. The explanation should say that.

check.summary: Both intended answers are correct. The 'Film and sound effects only' distractor in (a) is ambiguous because film does use sound effects. Why (b) wrongly suggests spoken description has no place in a podcast.
